Cached data can become stale. **Revalidation** refreshes it, either on a timer or when something changes.

<AppOnly>

This page covers the App Router.

</AppOnly>

<PagesOnly>

Pages Router users should read the getStaticProps guide instead.

</PagesOnly>

## Time-based revalidation

Pass `next.revalidate` to `fetch` to refresh the data at most once per interval, in seconds.

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
export default async function Page() {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/posts', { next: { revalidate: 60 } })
  const posts: Post[] = await res.json()
  return <PostList posts={posts} />
}
```

```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
export default async function Page() {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/posts', { next: { revalidate: 60 } })
  const posts = await res.json()
  return <PostList posts={posts} />
}
```

### Route segment config

You can also export `revalidate` from a layout or page to set the interval for every request in that segment.

| Option       | Type     | Default |
| ------------ | -------- | ------- |
| `revalidate` | `number` | `false` |

## On-demand revalidation

Call `revalidatePath` or `revalidateTag` from a Server Action or Route Handler after a mutation.

<Card title="revalidatePath" href="/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath" />

```ts filename="app/actions.ts"
'use server'

import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'

export async function createPost() {
  // ...save the post
  revalidatePath('/posts')
}
```
